stanzas.sanskrit:
अथ वारिणि घोरतरं फणिनं
प्रतिवारयितुं कृतधीर्भगवन् ।
द्रुतमारिथ तीरगनीपतरुं
विषमारुतशोषितपर्णचयम् ॥ ५५-१ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: With the intention to drive away Kaaliya from Yamuna river, Krishna reached the Kadamba tree near the bank of the river. The leaves of the tree had already dried up due to the poisonous air.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
atha vāriṇi ghorataraṃ phaṇinaṃ
prativārayituṃ kṛtadhīrbhagavan |
drutamāritha tīraganīpataruṃ
viṣamārutaśoṣitaparṇacayam || 55-1 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अधिरुह्य पदाम्बुरुहेण च तं
नवपल्लवतुल्यमनोज्ञरुचा ।
ह्रदवारिणि दूरतरं न्यपतः
परिघूर्णितघोरतरङ्गगणे ॥ ५५-२ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna climbed the tree with his lotus feet. From the top of the tree, He jumped into the river waters with swirling waves.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
adhiruhya padāmburuheṇa ca taṃ
navapallavatulyamanojñarucā |
hradavāriṇi dūrataraṃ nyapataḥ
parighūrṇitaghorataraṅgagaṇe || 55-2 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
भुवनत्रयभारभृतो भवतो
गुरुभारविकम्पिविजृम्भिजला ।
परिमज्जयति स्म धनुःशतकं
तटिनी झटिति स्फुटघोषवती ॥ ५५-३ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Krishna, who bears three worlds, when jumped in to the water, the river rose and swell due to his immense weight. The river bed submerged to an extent of hundred yards.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
bhuvanatrayabhārabhṛto bhavato
gurubhāravikampivijṛmbhijalā |
parimajjayati sma dhanuḥśatakaṃ
taṭinī jhaṭiti sphuṭaghoṣavatī || 55-3 ||

stanzas.commentary_en: The loud roaring sounds of water extended in all directions. Kaaliya was disturbed and angered by this sound. The serpent came out of the water angrily and rushed to Krishna.
The serpent Kaaliya came out of the water with thousand heads, each resembling like black mountains, emitting fire and deadly poison.

stanzas.sanskrit:
ज्वलदक्षिपरिक्षरदुग्रविष-
-श्वसनोष्मभरः स महाभुजगः ।
परिदश्य भवन्तमनन्तबलं
समवेष्टयदस्फुटचेष्टमहो ॥ ५५-६ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The serpent Kaaliya emitting deadly poison and breathing out intense heat, coiled around Krishna making Bhagwan’s body invisible.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jvaladakṣiparikṣaradugraviṣa-
-śvasanoṣmabharaḥ sa mahābhujagaḥ |
paridaśya bhavantamanantabalaṃ
samaveṣṭayadasphuṭaceṣṭamaho || 55-6 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अविलोक्य भवन्तमथाकुलिते
तटगामिनि बालकधेनुगणे ।
व्रजगेहतलेऽप्यनिमित्तशतं
समुदीक्ष्य गता यमुनां पशुपाः ॥ ५५-७ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: The Gopas became restless as they were waiting for Krishna and came in search near the river. Also the people of Vrindavan experienced some bad omens and rushed to river Yamuna to see what was happening there.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
avilokya bhavantamathākulite
taṭagāmini bālakadhenugaṇe |
vrajagehatale’pyanimittaśataṃ
samudīkṣya gatā yamunāṃ paśupāḥ || 55-7 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अखिलेषु विभो भवदीय दशा-
-मवलोक्य जिहासुषु जीवभरम् ।
फणिबन्धनमाशु विमुच्य जवा-
-दुदगम्यत हासजुषा भवता ॥ ५५-८ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: On seeing Krishna being surrounded by the deadly Kaaliya, the Gopas were gripped by fear and wanted to give up their life to save Krishna. But all of a sudden, Krishna quickly freed himself from the clutches of Kaaliya and emerged out smilingly.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
akhileṣu vibho bhavadīya daśā-
-mavalokya jihāsuṣu jīvabharam |
phaṇibandhanamāśu vimucya javā-
-dudagamyata hāsajuṣā bhavatā || 55-8 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
अधिरुह्य ततः फणिराजफणान्
ननृते भवता मृदुपादरुचा ।
कलशिञ्चितनूपुरमञ्जुमिल-
-त्करकङ्कणसङ्कुलसङ्क्वणितम् ॥ ५५-९ ॥
stanzas.commentary_en: Mounted on the hoods of the serpent Kaaliya, Krishna started to dance with his tender lotus like beautiful feet. He danced so beautifully over every rising hood of the serpent with his anklets making gentle sound matching with the tinklings of the bangles on his wrists.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
adhiruhya tataḥ phaṇirājaphaṇān
nanṛte bhavatā mṛdupādarucā |
kalaśiñcitanūpuramañjumila-
-tkarakaṅkaṇasaṅkulasaṅkvaṇitam || 55-9 ||

stanzas.sanskrit:
जहृषुः पशुपास्तुतुषुर्मुनयो
ववृषुः कुसुमानि सुरेन्द्रगणाः ।
त्वयि नृत्यति मारुतगेहपते
परिपाहि स मां त्वमदान्तगदात् ॥ ५५-१० ॥
stanzas.commentary_en:
Gopas were delighted to see the dance. Divine sages and Gods from heaven gathered to see Bhagwan’s dance and showered flowers.

Bhattathiri prayed to Guruvayoorappan to protect him and cure him from his illness.
stanzas.stanza_roman:
jahṛṣuḥ paśupāstutuṣurmunayo
vavṛṣuḥ kusumāni surendragaṇāḥ |
tvayi nṛtyati mārutagehapate
paripāhi sa māṃ tvamadāntagadāt || 55-10 ||
